label: Take the tour (60 seconds)

steps.caption: Winter half, Sun only: 14,098 measured areas get at least 100 hours of two-hour spells under the Malapert Massif ceiling.
On snow-free ground, only 15 of these areas keep 100 hours in the winter half.
Summer half: 3,145 measured areas keep at least 100 hours after snow and hills.
Under typical cloud, the median area keeps 24 percent of those hours. 238 areas still have at least 50 hours.
Connecting Ridge has the lowest Sun ceiling, 2.08 degrees. Its two-hour spells start only at 64.8 degrees north.
Devon Island, Haughton crater: its area keeps 102 hours a year of two-hour spells for Malapert Massif after snow and hills.
Antarctica: snow on rock is not measured. Thus, only the rock season counts, from 27 November to 1 March. We rank 617 areas there.
None of the 11 lower-latitude analog sites has a two-hour spell. For Malapert Massif, snow removes the most hours at 10 of 12 named Arctic sites.

reduced_motion: If reduced motion is on, the tour waits until the reader presses Next.
seconds_what: Each tour stop gets 5 seconds. The page divides the rest of the minute by the length of each caption.
